title: Context of Scripture
definition: The context of Scripture is the surrounding setting, argument, book, covenantal moment, and biblical storyline that helps readers understand a passage rightly.
summary: Verses should not be isolated from the passage, book, or message in which God gave them.
christFocus: Christ-centered interpretation respects context while seeing how each passage fits within God's saving work in Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Context of Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to context of scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
